transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

For almost two years, I’ve been certain that certain people in the music scene are secretly coordinating to destroy my career, and nothing anyone says changes that. Everyone else just tells me I'm overreacting or imagining things, but the coordination against me is absolutely real.
Have you experienced any periods where you didn't believe in this coordination against you, or has this belief been constant over the past two years?

No, it has been completely constant and unshakeable since it first started nearly two years ago. I haven't had a single moment of doubt, even though my wife and bandmates keep trying to convince me I'm wrong. The patterns and evidence are just too clear for me to ignore.
Have you experienced any other unusual perceptions, such as hearing voices or seeing things that others can't, in addition to your belief about the music scene?
No, I have never heard voices or seen things that aren't there. My mind is completely clear, and my only issue is the very real coordination against me in the music scene.
Can you tell me more about what specific actions or events you've observed in the music scene that make you so certain about this coordination against you?

It all started after a major grant of mine was rejected; suddenly, a festival "lost" my score, a conductor took days to reply to simple emails, and routine scheduling changes kept happening. While others dismiss these things as bad luck or disorganization, I am certain these are deliberate actions coordinated by my old professor and a few colleagues in the local new-music circle to blacklist me.

Have you noticed any significant impairment in your social or occupational functioning as a result of this belief, or have you been able to maintain your daily life and relationships relatively normally despite this conviction?

For the most part, my day-to-day routine is normal—I still write music on deadline, run rehearsals smoothly, and pay my bills on time. However, it has caused serious issues; I've turned down collaborations and almost walked away from a major residency because I was convinced it was a trap. Plus, some ensemble leaders have stopped calling me for gigs after I confronted them about their involvement in this scheme.
Have you ever taken any actions to counteract or investigate this perceived coordination against you, such as gathering evidence or confronting the individuals you believe are involved?

Yes, I’ve spent countless late nights combing through past reviews and social media to compile evidence and connect the dots. I also confronted administrators and a couple of ensemble leaders about their involvement, which unfortunately led to them stopping calling me for gigs. I've even had to protect myself by turning down collaborations and almost walking away from a major residency because I knew they were traps.

Have you ever felt that your thoughts are being controlled, inserted, or broadcasted to others, or have you experienced any other unusual thoughts or experiences beyond this specific belief about the music scene?

No, absolutely not. My thoughts are entirely my own, and I have never experienced anything like thought control or broadcasting. My focus is strictly on the very real, coordinated effort by my former professor and colleagues to sabotage my career.

Have you considered seeking legal action or involving law enforcement to address what you believe is a coordinated effort against you, or have you taken any other concrete steps to formally investigate or expose this perceived conspiracy?

I haven't gone to the police or hired a lawyer yet, but I’ve taken concrete steps to gather evidence on my own by spending late nights combing through emails, past reviews, and social media. I’ve also directly confronted university administrators and several ensemble leaders to expose their involvement in this scheme. I want to make sure I have all my proof completely lined up first.

Have you ever experienced any significant distress or impairment in your daily life due to this belief, beyond the professional setbacks you've mentioned, such as problems with sleep, appetite, or mood that you attribute to this situation?

My physical health, appetite, and basic routine like writing music on deadline and paying bills are completely normal. However, whenever an email or meeting touches on those people, I get completely derailed and spend late nights obsessively combing through social media and reviews for evidence. While I don't have a mood disorder, this constant investigation is what truly disrupts my peace of mind and my relationship with my wife.
